about.title: About Heart Rate Calculator - Training Zone Reference
about.description: The Heart Rate Calculator estimates target heart rate zones for different exercise intensities based on age, resting heart rate, and selected training inputs. It can help you review training zones for cardio, endurance, and general fitness planning, but the output is still formula-based and may not reflect individual medical conditions or performance testing. Use it as a workout-planning reference, and seek qualified guidance for health-specific decisions.

faq.q: What is target heart rate and why is it important?
faq.a: Target heart rate is a reference range used during exercise to help gauge training intensity for different fitness goals. It is typically expressed as a percentage of your estimated maximum heart rate and can be used as a planning guide rather than an individualized medical threshold.

faq.q: How do I measure my resting heart rate?
faq.a: Measure your pulse for 60 seconds immediately after waking up, before getting out of bed or consuming caffeine. Take measurements for several consecutive days and use the average. Resting heart rate ranges can vary across individuals and situations.

faq.q: What's the fat burning zone and how effective is it?
faq.a: The fat burning zone is typically 60-70% of maximum heart rate, where your body primarily uses fat for energy. While this zone uses a higher percentage of fat for fuel, higher intensities burn more total calories and can be more effective for weight loss.

faq.q: Is it safe to exercise at maximum heart rate?
faq.a: Exercising at maximum heart rate should only be done by well-trained athletes for short periods during interval training. Most people should stay within 50-85% of maximum heart rate for safe and effective exercise. Consult healthcare providers before high-intensity training.
